comments.body:
EVIDENCE — the code-verifiable criteria are met; ONE criterion legitimately awaits a live harness run.

MERGED as Gerrit change 1118, in origin/main at 09be45933 (content confirmed:
`git show origin/main:tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_fetcher_pagination_heldout.py` resolves).

THE REPRODUCTION, BEFORE AND AFTER. A client serving 250 issues while capping every page at 20 (a
lowered `jira.search.views.default.max`, the documented DC hardening):

    before: 20 of 250 recovered  — 92% of the inbound snapshot silently lost
    after : 250 of 250 recovered

Run against `fetcher.collect(..., page_size=100)` directly, not inferred from the diff.

PER-CRITERION
 * "the 250/20 reproduction recovers 250, asserted by a held-out unit test that FAILS on the current
   code" — MET. `test_a_server_capped_page_does_not_end_the_scan`; confirmed RED before the fix
   (recovered 20) and green after.
 * "termination is on an EMPTY page only, and the advance is by `len(page)`" — MET, readable at
   `fetcher.py`'s pager: `start_at += len(page)`, with the early `if not page: return` as the sole
   terminator.
 * "a `startAt`-ignoring server raises `SilentTruncationError` instead of looping, with a bounded-time
   guarantee" — MET, `test_a_server_that_ignores_start_at_on_a_full_page_raises_rather_than_looping`
   (bounded at 100 calls so a hang fails the test rather than the suite).
 * "the existing `cap`, ACLI-ceiling and `same-token-twice` behaviours are unchanged, each asserted by
   a test that exercises them" — MET, four tests. This mattered: `cap` was ALSO broken by the original
   defect (`cap=45` yielded 20, because truncation ended the scan before the cap was reached), which
   the cap test caught and which I had not predicted.
 * "the full unit suite passes" — MET locally: 1720 passed in tests/unit/rebar_reconciler, plus lint
   and mypy clean. NOTE the caveat now recorded in the handoff: local pytest is NOT a faithful CI
   oracle on this machine (CI runs py3.11; this host has only 3.13/3.14). The authoritative signal is
   the Verified +1 this change received before submit.
 * "the live DC harness job stays green" — **NOT YET MET, and correctly so.** No harness run has
   executed against a main containing this change. A run is queued behind changes 1124 and 1127; I
   will record the run id and the JOB result (not the overall run status) here before re-closing.

TWO DESIGN CORRECTIONS MADE DURING IMPLEMENTATION, recorded because both were caught by tests rather
than by review:
 1. The first offset-stall guard raised on ANY repeated page, which broke seven existing tests whose
    doubles ignore `startAt` entirely. Narrowed to: a repeated FULL page raises (the server claims
    more while never advancing, so the loop would never terminate), a repeated SHORT page stops
    cleanly (an offset-blind client with nothing left to give). This does not weaken the fix — a
    hardened DC honours `startAt`, so its second capped page holds DIFFERENT issues and the scan
    continues.
 2. The stall check initially ran AFTER the yield, so the duplicate page reached the caller and drove
    duplicate creates in a dry-run pass that must write nothing. Moved before the yield. Caught only
    because two orchestration tests assert "writes nothing".

compiled_state.description:
## Evidence — reproduced, not inferred

`fetcher._iter_pages` (the pager behind `fetcher.collect`, which builds the INBOUND SNAPSHOT the
entire inbound differ runs on) terminates on a SHORT page and advances by the REQUESTED page size:

    src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/fetcher.py:324-326
        if len(page) < page_size:
            return
        start_at += page_size

Jira Data Center silently truncates `maxResults` when it exceeds `jira.search.views.default.max` — a
common hardening, and the same server behaviour already established for this codebase when the
identical defect was fixed in `get_parent_map` (change 1105). A truncated FIRST page therefore reads
as "that is all there is".

Measured against a client that serves 250 issues but caps every page at 20 (default `page_size=100`):

    issues recovered: 20 of 250
    CONFIRMED DEFECT: 230 issues (92%) silently lost from the inbound snapshot

## Why this is more serious than its two siblings

This is the THIRD instance of one defect class. The first was `get_parent_map` (fixed, change 1105).
The second is [rebar:9263-b404-cb6c-463f] — `get_issuelinks_map` / `get_comment_map`, which lose links
and comments. This one loses THE ISSUES THEMSELVES.

`collect()` feeds `_build_snapshot`, so a truncated read is not a missing attribute on a present
issue — it is an issue the pass never sees at all. Every unseen bound issue is a candidate for the
absence/deletion path, and every unseen unbound issue simply fails to reconcile. A run in that state
reports success: it raises nothing, and "converged" is true of the 8% it looked at.

## Blast radius — wider than the DC adapter, which is why this is NOT folded into 9263

9263 is confined to `adapters/jira_datacenter/transport.py`. This is CORE `fetcher.py`, on the shared
inbound path, so a change here reaches the live Cloud bridge as well as DC. That is a different risk
profile and deserves its own review and its own live verification rather than riding along on an
adapter-local fix.

Cloud reaches the same lines but is not known to be affected in practice: its ceiling and
`same-token-twice` cursor-stall guards target a different truncation mode, and no short-page
truncation has been observed there. The fix must therefore be verified as SAFE FOR CLOUD, not merely
correct for DC.

## Approach

Advance by `len(page)` and terminate only on an EMPTY page — the same correction already applied to
`get_parent_map`, whose docstring records the reasoning.

One thing the `get_parent_map` fix did not have to handle and this one does: `_iter_pages` must not
spin forever if a server ignores `startAt` and returns the same non-empty page indefinitely. The
existing `same-token-twice` guard covers the Cloud CURSOR stall, not an OFFSET stall. Add an
offset-stall guard that raises `SilentTruncationError` (the type this function already raises for
truncation it refuses to hide) rather than looping.

`cap` and ceiling semantics are unchanged.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/fetcher.py` — the pager's advance/terminate conditions, plus the
  offset-stall guard.
- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/` — held-out regression tests.

## Testing

- a client serving N issues while capping every page below the requested size yields ALL N (the
  reproduction above, which currently returns 20 of 250)
- an exactly-full final page followed by an empty page terminates without an extra spurious request
- a server that ignores `startAt` raises `SilentTruncationError` rather than looping forever
- `cap` still clips, and the ACLI ceiling still raises — asserted so the Cloud contract is pinned
  unchanged by this fix

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] the 250-issue/20-cap reproduction recovers 250, asserted by a held-out unit test that FAILS on
      the current code
- [ ] termination is on an EMPTY page only, and the advance is by `len(page)` — read from the source
- [ ] a `startAt`-ignoring server raises `SilentTruncationError` instead of looping, asserted by test
      with a bounded-time guarantee
- [ ] the existing `cap`, ACLI-ceiling and `same-token-twice` behaviours are unchanged, each asserted
      by a test that exercises them — this touches the shared Cloud path, so "DC is fixed" is not
      sufficient evidence
- [ ] the full unit suite passes, and the live DC harness job stays green

file_impact.reason: fix the pager advance/terminate conditions and add an offset-stall guard
held-out regression tests incl. the Cloud-contract pins
